# plugin-hostd

A daemon that hosts CLAP and LV2 audio plugins out of process, each in a worker of its own, behind mod-host's command protocol: its command parser and dispatcher, and the relay of its workers' feedback to the controller. [FreeMixer/plugin-hostd](https://github.com/FreeMixer/plugin-hostd) · OSS-Fuzz: no project for plugin-hostd

**Status: available.** Of plugin-hostd's own fuzz targets, which OSS-Fuzz does not run, statements cover 2 of 2. 8 binaries, 2.7 MB. 14 statements: 14 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 0 open.

Built from plugin-hostd 0.10.0 (commit `65cd2b02`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz_command](fuzz_command/) | Reads the input as up to 32 messages, each a flags byte, a two-byte length and up to 8192 bytes, copies each into an allocation of exactly its length and hands it to verbs_receive, plugin-hostd's command parser and dispatcher. A recorder stands in for the supervisor, the pins, the descriptor scans and the socket: it records every call and, as the flags byte chooses, accepts it with the verb's declared reply or refuses it with a declared error code. After each message the harness checks the reply and the calls, then sends the message again as its words joined by one space. | 6 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle, roundtrip; 1 weak; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_reply](fuzz_reply/) | Opens one worker feedback source in plugin-hostd's relay, src/relay.c, then reads the input as up to 512 operations: add a source (at most four), have a source write bytes, read a source, close or remove a source, remove an instance, interrupt a receive, send an event of the daemon's own, limit or interrupt the controller's sends, or make the controller go away. Its own recv and send stand in for the sockets, so no socket or thread is used. A reference splitter follows what each source wrote. At the end the relay is shut down. | 8 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle; 1 weak; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |

## What the statements say, for plugin-hostd
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch plugin-hostd
    ./oft verify-sha plugin-hostd

By hand: download `plugin-hostd-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.11.1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1), unpack it into `projects/plugin-hostd/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; a testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [FreeMixer/plugin-hostd](https://github.com/FreeMixer/plugin-hostd) at `65cd2b02e8306f7e5f98fa0adfd0b3f8c1df6a5c` (0.10.0), built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. The OSS Verify port `projects/plugin-hostd` at `2840abf10963080bf3ef5a52a2af576aef8d1f8f` in `theorem-labs/oss-verify` built every binary of this project instead of a build recipe. Its archive [`plugin-hostd-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src) holds the port's `tools/check`, which builds them again on this image with Docker: it fetches the project's source trees over the network, at the commits and SHA-256s the port pins, and does not read `plugin-hostd-src.tar.zst` ([docs/reproducing.md](../../docs/reproducing.md)).

Each binary is a combined work of plugin-hostd, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet.
